head: claude/mi113-pending-pings-merge-driver
title: MI-113: arm merge=union on pending-pings.jsonl (jsonregister measured and rejected)
body:
> ⚠️ **THE LIVE PR BODY ON #11024 IS STALE AND THIS FILE IS THE CORRECTED RECORD.**
> `pr-opener` writes the body once (the result file is the idempotency key), and this session
> cannot edit it afterwards — `update_pull_request` and `add_issue_comment` both return
> `403 Resource not accessible by integration`, the sub-session permissions asymmetry
> `.github/pr-landing/README.md` records. The Guards section published on #11024 reported
> `PASS 63 · FAIL 2`, calling both failures environmental. That was wrong and is corrected
> below. Read this file's body, not the PR's.

`docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl` has no merge driver, so every ping-carrying PR conflicts on it unresolvably. The only two exits are close-the-PR — which silently drops an operator-facing ping — and hand-rescuing the rows, which is what #10974 did for five of them.

## The measurement

Population: the **full set of five** ping-carrying PRs whose conflict was observed 2026-09-04 — #10888, #10902, #10908, #10914, #10926. Each test-merged into **current `origin/main` @5eb59917** in a throwaway worktree, with `merge.jsonregister` **armed** in every arm:

| `.gitattributes` | conflicts | merged file, read |
|---|---|---|
| no mapping (today) | **5/5** | both sides' text, inside conflict markers |
| `merge=jsonregister` | **5/5** | ⚠️ the PR's ping row is **not in the file at all** |
| `merge=union` | **0/5** | both sides' rows present |

Read, not inferred: merging #10888 into current `main` gives 91 lines / 90 unique, with every one of `main`'s 90 rows present and every one of the PR's 61 present.

**Pre-rescue positive control.** Against current `main` these PRs have **zero** PR-only rows, because #10974 already rescued them — so the interesting case had to be reconstructed. Re-running against `b95ac61f` (`main` *before* #10974), where each row still existed **only** on the PR side: `union` merged 74 + 1 → 75 rows clean, with the PR-only row present in all 5/5. Under `jsonregister` the same 5/5 conflicted **and the file held 74 rows with no markers** — the ping simply gone, so a `git add` on that path drops it. That is why jsonregister here is worse than doing nothing.

## Why jsonregister was rejected

It was **run**, not assumed. It parses the file as one JSON document, so appended *lines* read to it as disagreeing header scalars and it refuses — correct instinct, wrong file. Nobody had ever run it against JSONL; it does not handle it.

## Why union is safe here — the objection was tested

`union` resurrects deletions, and a drained ping could in principle be deleted. It is not. `notify_on_pull.py::_drain_pending_pings` **leaves the file in place** and dedupes by line hash via `runtime_logs/pending_pings_delivered.txt` (gitignored, per-clone); its docstring says this replaced the old truncate-in-a-follow-up-commit contract.

Over the file's whole history: **94 commits** touch it, **4** show deletions. Three predate the dedupe contract (`350cc391`, 2026-05-06) and *were* that old contract. The only post-contract one (`39e6cbe0`) is a pure reflow — 22 lines removed, all 22 re-added byte-identical, **0 rows semantically gone**. So across 90 post-contract commits nothing has ever removed a row, and union has nothing to resurrect.

## What union costs, stated rather than glossed

A row hand-rescued onto `main` by value duplicates when its PR later merges — #10888 into current `main` duplicates the `2026-09-03T04:44:40` `night_shift_summary` row byte-for-byte. That is **one duplicate operator page**, because the hash ledger dedupes *across* drain passes but not *within* one: `_drain_pending_pings` never adds to `delivered` as it iterates, so two identical lines return two pings (measured: 2 pings, 1 distinct hash). Filed rather than fixed — `notify_on_pull.py` is outside this change's scope.

A duplicate page is noise and recoverable. A dropped ping is loss and is not. That is the trade this line takes, deliberately.

## The test

`tests/ops/test_pending_pings_merge_union.py` runs **real three-way `git merge`s in throwaway repos**, not fixtures, and **reads the merged file** rather than inferring union from a zero exit code (`-X ours` also produces no conflict while dropping the other side's ping). It carries a positive control — without the mapping, the same two appends conflict — and pins union's known delete-resurrection behaviour so it is a decision and not a surprise. 4 passed; ruff clean.

## Landing is `hold`, against the dispatch instruction

This session was told to self-land as Tier-1 with both landing files. **That is not possible, and the allowlist was not widened to make it possible.** `pr-landing-guard` R5 refuses to self-land a diff containing `.gitattributes`, which is outside `TIER1_SURFACE`. Editing the guard that judges this PR is the *"cheaper to lie to than to satisfy"* failure `check_pr_landing.py`'s own docstring warns about, so a human decides that, not me. The auto-merge request file was removed and `landing` is `hold`.

The `hold_reason` token is imperfect and says so in its own first line: no operator spoke, and none of the five closed-vocabulary reasons is true for this case. Following the precedent mi102 and mi95 set for a knowingly-approximate token — and filed as a gap.

## Filed, not fixed

Both via `backlog_append.py::append_row`:

- `BL-20260905-PENDING-PINGS-WITHIN-PASS-DUPLICATE` — the ledger dedupes across drain passes but not within one.
- `BL-20260905-PR-LANDING-VOCAB-HAS-NO-UNVOUCHED-PATH-HOLD` — R5 forces a hold that R7's vocabulary cannot express.

## Guards

`python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` → **PASS 65 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 22**, with `requirements-dev.txt` installed so the run matches CI. `pytest tests/ops/test_pending_pings_merge_union.py` → 4 passed. `ruff check .` clean.

⚠️ **An earlier revision of this body reported "FAIL 2, both environmental, identical on `origin/main`" and that reading was wrong — recording it rather than quietly reporting the second number.** Two things were being conflated. `layer-guard` exiting 127 genuinely was environmental (`lint-imports` was not installed); that is *"could not measure"*, not a finding, and it passes once `import-linter` is in. But the ruff failure was **not** environmental: the sandbox had ruff **0.16.6** while `requirements-dev.txt` pins **0.15.x**, and under 0.16's expanded default ruleset the whole repo reports ~15050 findings — which swamped the count and made "15050 on main, 15050 on the branch, so this diff adds zero" look like a clean subtraction. Under the **pinned** ruff the repo is clean and the branch had exactly **one real finding, in my own new file** (`E731`, a `lambda` assignment). It is fixed — now a named `_canon` helper. The lesson is the one this repo keeps writing down: a difference of two large numbers is not a measurement of the small thing, and an unpinned tool is a different tool.

## Scope

Tier-1. `.gitattributes` + one test + two backlog rows + the landing declaration. No `src/`, `config/`, `deploy/`, workflow, order path, or VM mutation. A git merge driver is **client-side only** — GitHub does not run it, so this does not make a `dirty` ping PR auto-mergeable; it removes the hand-rescue cost for whoever holds the clone. `union` is a git built-in, so unlike `jsonregister` it needs no installer and works in a clone that never ran `install_merge_driver.sh`.

## Note on the work object

`docs/claude/work/objects/WO-20260905-PENDING-PINGS-HAS-NO-MERGE-DRIVER-SO-PING-PRS-DIE.yaml` **does not exist** on `main` or on this branch — no `WO-20260905-*` file matches at all. The dispatch prompt carried the measurement, done_condition and trap, so this was built from that; flagging it so the gap is visible rather than assumed handled.
